Latin word

repercutiō

repercutiō, repercutere, repercussī, repercussum

verb, third conjugation

reflect, throw back (light, an image, a sound)

In this lexicon

  • reflect

    the recommended word · classical · Verg. A. 8.23: lūmen … sōle repercussum; Ov. Met. 3.434: repercussae … imāginis

Examples

  • sīcut aquae tremulum labrīs ubi lūmen aēnīs sōle repercussum aut radiantis imāgine lūnae omnia pervolitat lātē loca, jamque sub aurās ērigitur summīque ferit laqueāria tēctī

    as when the trembling light of water in bronze basins, thrown back by the sun or by the image of the shining moon, flits far and wide over everything, rises into the air and strikes the panels of the ceiling high aboveVerg. A. 8.22–25

    In the entry for reflect

  • canis per flūmen carnem cum ferret natāns lymphārum in speculō vīdit simulācrum suum

    a dog swimming across a river with a piece of meat saw his reflection in the mirror of the waterPhaedr. 1.4.2–3

    In the entry for reflect

  • ista repercussae, quam cernis, imāginis umbra est

    what you see is the shadow of a reflected imageOv. Met. 3.434
